d: The sex-determining region of the Y chromosome. It encodes testis-determining factor, a transcription factor that turns the supporting cells of the indifferent gonad into Sertoli cells.

A hormone from fetal Sertoli cells that makes the paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct on its own side regress. Its absence, or a receptor defect, causes persistent Müllerian duct syndrome. After puberty, granulosa cells of small follicles make it, so its level estimates ovarian reserve.
A cyst in the lateral wall of the vagina formed from a remnant of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct, which normally regresses in females.
A cord of tissue from the lower pole of the gonad to the labioscrotal swelling. It guides testicular descent in males and becomes the ovarian and round ligaments in females.
The pouch of peritoneum that precedes the testis through the inguinal canal. Its distal part becomes the tunica vaginalis, and failure to close causes an indirect hernia or communicating hydrocele.
Müllerian agenesis in a 46,XX patient: normal ovaries, breasts and pubic hair, but no uterus or upper vagina. It causes primary amenorrhea, and renal anomalies are common.
A transcription factor that SRY switches on in the supporting cells of the gonad. It makes them Sertoli cells and drives AMH, and its loss causes 46,XY sex reversal with campomelic dysplasia.

Insulin-like factor 3, a hormone from fetal Leydig cells. It swells the gubernaculum and holds the testis near the deep inguinal ring in the first phase of descent, and its loss can leave the testis undescended.
